88:     let payment_method_data = SplitPaymentMethodDataRequest {
89:         payment_method_data: request
90:             .payment_method_data
91:             .payment_method_data
92:             .clone()
93:             .ok_or(errors::ApiErrorResponse::MissingRequiredField {
94:                 field_name: "payment_method_data",
95:             })?,
96:         payment_method_type: request.payment_method_type,
97:         payment_method_subtype: request.payment_method_subtype,
98:     };
99: 
100:     let combined_pm_data: Vec<_> = split_payment_method_data
101:         .into_iter()
102:         .chain(std::iter::once(payment_method_data))
103:         .collect();
104: 
105:     let (gift_card_pm_data, non_gift_card_pm_data): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = combined_pm_data
106:         .into_iter()
107:         .partition(|pm_data| pm_data.payment_method_type.is_gift_card());
108: 
109:     // Validate at most one non-gift-card payment method
110:     if non_gift_card_pm_data.len() > 1 {
111:         Err(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InvalidRequestData {
112:             message: "At most one non-gift card payment method is allowed".to_string(),
113:         })?
114:     }
115: 
116:     // It is possible that non-gift card payment method is not present, e.g. only 2 gift cards were provided
117:     let non_gift_card_pm_data = non_gift_card_pm_data.into_iter().next();
118: 
119:     let gift_card_data_vec = gift_card_pm_data
120:         .iter()
121:         .map(|elem| {
122:             if let PaymentMethodData::GiftCard(gift_card_data) = elem.payment_method_data.clone() {
123:                 Ok(gift_card_data.as_ref().clone())
124:             } else {
125:                 Err(report!(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InvalidRequestData {
126:                     message: "Only Gift Card supported for Split Payments".to_string(),
127:                 }))
128:             }
129:         })
130:         .collect::<RouterResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
131: 
132:     let balance_check_data_vec = gift_card_data_vec
133:         .iter()
134:         .cloned()
135:         .map(api_models::payments::BalanceCheckPaymentMethodData::GiftCard)
136:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
137: 
138:     let balances = payment_method_balance::fetch_payment_methods_balances_from_redis(
139:         state,
140:         payment_id,
141:         &balance_check_data_vec,
142:     )
143:     .await?;
144: 
145:     // TODO: Add surcharge calculation when it is added in v2
146:     let total_amount = payment_intent.amount_details.calculate_net_amount();
147: 
148:     let mut remaining_to_allocate = total_amount;
149:     let pm_split_amt_tuple: Vec<(PaymentMethodData, MinorUnit)> = gift_card_data_vec
150:         .iter()
151:         .filter_map(|gift_card_card| {
152:             if remaining_to_allocate == MinorUnit::zero() {
153:                 return None; // Payment already fully covered
154:             }
155: 
156:             let pm_balance_key = domain::PaymentMethodBalanceKey {
157:                 payment_method_type: common_enums::PaymentMethod::GiftCard,
158:                 payment_method_subtype: gift_card_card.get_payment_method_type(),
159:                 payment_method_key: domain::GiftCardData::from(gift_card_card.clone())
160:                     .get_payment_method_key()
161:                     .change_context(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InvalidRequestData {
162:                         message: "Unable to get unique key for payment method".to_string(),
163:                     })
164:                     .ok()?
165:                     .expose(),
166:             };
167: 
168:             let pm_balance = balances
169:                 .get(&pm_balance_key)
170:                 .ok_or(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
171:                 .attach_printable("Payment Method Balance not present in Redis")
172:                 .ok()?;
173: 
174:             // Use minimum of available balance and remaining amount
175:             let amount_to_use = pm_balance.balance.min(remaining_to_allocate);
176:             remaining_to_allocate = remaining_to_allocate - amount_to_use;
177: 
178:             Some(Ok((
179:                 PaymentMethodData::GiftCard(Box::new(gift_card_card.to_owned())),
180:                 amount_to_use,
181:             )))
182:         })
183:         .collect::<RouterResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
184: 
185:     // If the gift card balances are not sufficient for payment, use the non-gift card payment method
186:     // for the remaining amount
187:     if remaining_to_allocate > MinorUnit::zero() {
188:         let non_gift_card_pm_data = non_gift_card_pm_data
189:             .ok_or(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InvalidRequestData {
190:                 message: "Requires additional payment method data".to_string(),
191:             })?
192:             .payment_method_data;
193: 
194:         Ok(split_payments::PaymentMethodAmountSplit {
195:             balance_pm_split: pm_split_amt_tuple,
196:             non_balance_pm_split: Some((non_gift_card_pm_data, remaining_to_allocate)),
197:         })
198:     } else {
199:         Ok(split_payments::PaymentMethodAmountSplit {
200:             balance_pm_split: pm_split_amt_tuple,
201:             non_balance_pm_split: None,
202:         })
203:     }
204: }

206: pub(crate) async fn split_payments_execute_core(
207:     state: SessionState,
208:     req_state: ReqState,
209:     platform: domain::Platform,
210:     profile: domain::Profile,
211:     request: payments_api::PaymentsConfirmIntentRequest,
212:     header_payload: HeaderPayload,
213:     payment_id: id_type::GlobalPaymentId,
214: ) -> RouterResponse<payments_api::PaymentsResponse> {
215:     let db = &*state.store;
216: 
217:     let payment_intent = db
218:         .find_payment_intent_by_id(
219:             &payment_id,
220:             platform.get_processor().get_key_store(),
221:             platform.get_processor().get_account().storage_scheme,
222:         )
223:         .await
224:         .to_not_found_response(errors::ApiErrorResponse::PaymentNotFound)?;
225: 
226:     if !payment_intent.supports_split_payments() {
227:         Err(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InvalidRequestData {
228:             message: "Split Payments not enabled in Payment Intent".to_string(),
229:         })?
230:     }
231: 
232:     let cell_id = state.conf.cell_information.id.clone();
233: 
234:     let attempts_group_id = id_type::GlobalAttemptGroupId::generate(&cell_id);
235: 
236:     // Change the active_attempt_id_type of PaymentIntent to `GroupID`. This indicates that the customer
237:     // has attempted a split payment for this intent
238:     let payment_intent_update =
239:         hyperswitch_domain_models::payments::payment_intent::PaymentIntentUpdate::AttemptGroupUpdate {
240:             updated_by: platform
241:                 .get_processor()
242:                 .get_account()
243:                 .storage_scheme
244:                 .to_string(),
245:             active_attempt_id_type: enums::ActiveAttemptIDType::GroupID,
246:             active_attempts_group_id: attempts_group_id.clone(),
247:         };
248: 
249:     let payment_intent = db
250:         .update_payment_intent(
251:             payment_intent,
252:             payment_intent_update,
253:             platform.get_processor().get_key_store(),
254:             platform.get_processor().get_account().storage_scheme,
255:         )
256:         .await
257:         .change_context(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
258:         .attach_printable("Unable to update payment intent")?;
259: 
260:     let pm_amount_split =
261:         get_payment_method_amount_split(&state, &payment_id, &request, &payment_intent).await?;
262: 
263:     let (
264:         primary_pm_response,
265:         connector_http_status_code,
266:         external_latency,
267:         connector_response_data,
268:     ) = {
269:         // If a non-balance Payment Method is present, we will execute that first, otherwise we will execute
270:         // a balance Payment Method
271:         let (payment_method_data, amount) = pm_amount_split
272:             .non_balance_pm_split
273:             .clone()
274:             .or_else(|| pm_amount_split.balance_pm_split.first().cloned())
275:             .get_required_value("payment method amount split")
276:             .change_context(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
277:             .attach_printable("At least one payment method is required")?;
278: 
279:         let operation = PaymentIntentConfirm;
280: 
281:         let get_tracker_response: operations::GetTrackerResponse<
282:             PaymentConfirmData<api::Authorize>,
283:         > = operation
284:             .to_get_tracker()?
285:             .get_trackers_for_split_payments(
286:                 &state,
287:                 &payment_id,
288:                 &request,
289:                 &platform,
290:                 &profile,
291:                 &header_payload,
292:                 (payment_method_data, amount),
293:                 &attempts_group_id,
294:             )
295:             .await?;
296: 
297:         let (
298:             payment_data,
299:             _req,
300:             _customer,
301:             connector_http_status_code,
302:             external_latency,
303:             connector_response_data,
304:         ) = Box::pin(payments_operation_core(
305:             &state,
306:             req_state.clone(),
307:             platform.clone(),
308:             &profile,
309:             operation,
310:             request.clone(),
311:             get_tracker_response,
312:             CallConnectorAction::Trigger,
313:             header_payload.clone(),
314:         ))
315:         .await?;
316: 
317:         // payments_operation_core marks the intent as succeeded when the attempt is succesful
318:         // However, for split case, we can't mark the intent as succesful until all the attempts
319:         // have succeeded, so reverting the state of Payment Intent
320:         if payment_data.payment_intent.is_succeeded() {
321:             let payment_intent_update =
322:             hyperswitch_domain_models::payments::payment_intent::PaymentIntentUpdate::SplitPaymentStatusUpdate {
323:                 status: common_enums::IntentStatus::RequiresPaymentMethod,
324:                 updated_by: platform
325:                     .get_processor()
326:                     .get_account()
327:                     .storage_scheme
328:                     .to_string(),
329:             };
330: 
331:             let updated_payment_intent = db
332:                 .update_payment_intent(
333:                     payment_data.payment_intent.clone(),
334:                     payment_intent_update,
335:                     platform.get_processor().get_key_store(),
336:                     platform.get_processor().get_account().storage_scheme,
337:                 )
338:                 .await
339:                 .change_context(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
340:                 .attach_printable("Unable to update payment intent")?;
341:         }
342: 
343:         (
344:             payment_data,
345:             connector_http_status_code,
346:             external_latency,
347:             connector_response_data,
348:         )
349:     };
350: 
351:     let mut split_pm_response_data = SplitPaymentResponseData {
352:         primary_payment_response_data: primary_pm_response,
353:         secondary_payment_response_data: vec![],
354:     };
355: 
356:     // We have executed the primary payment method, now get a vector of the secondary payment methods
357:     // If we had a non-balance payment method, it was executed first, so the remaining ones are the balance PMs
358:     // otherwise the first balance payment method was executed, so remove it from the remaining PMs
359:     let remaining_pm_amount_split = if pm_amount_split.non_balance_pm_split.is_some() {
360:         pm_amount_split.balance_pm_split
361:     } else {
362:         pm_amount_split
363:             .balance_pm_split
364:             .iter()
365:             .skip(1)
366:             .cloned()
367:             .collect()
368:     };
369: 
370:     for (payment_method_data, amount) in remaining_pm_amount_split {
371:         let operation = PaymentIntentConfirm;
372: 
373:         let get_tracker_response: operations::GetTrackerResponse<
374:             PaymentConfirmData<api::Authorize>,
375:         > = operation
376:             .to_get_tracker()?
377:             .get_trackers_for_split_payments(
378:                 &state,
379:                 &payment_id,
380:                 &request,
381:                 &platform,
382:                 &profile,
383:                 &header_payload,
384:                 (payment_method_data.to_owned(), amount.to_owned()),
385:                 &attempts_group_id,
386:             )
387:             .await?;
388: 
389:         let (
390:             payment_data,
391:             _req,
392:             _customer,
393:             _connector_http_status_code,
394:             _external_latency,
395:             _connector_response_data,
396:         ) = Box::pin(payments_operation_core(
397:             &state,
398:             req_state.clone(),
399:             platform.clone(),
400:             &profile,
401:             operation,
402:             request.clone(),
403:             get_tracker_response,
404:             CallConnectorAction::Trigger,
405:             header_payload.clone(),
406:         ))
407:         .await?;
408: 
409:         // payments_operation_core marks the intent as succeeded when the attempt is succesful
410:         // However, for split case, we can't mark the intent as succesful until all the attempts
411:         // have succeeded, so reverting the state of Payment Intent
412:         if payment_data.payment_intent.is_succeeded() {
413:             let payment_intent_update =
414:             hyperswitch_domain_models::payments::payment_intent::PaymentIntentUpdate::SplitPaymentStatusUpdate {
415:                 status: common_enums::IntentStatus::RequiresPaymentMethod,
416:                 updated_by: platform
417:                     .get_processor()
418:                     .get_account()
419:                     .storage_scheme
420:                     .to_string(),
421:             };
422: 
423:             let _updated_payment_intent = db
424:                 .update_payment_intent(
425:                     payment_data.payment_intent.clone(),
426:                     payment_intent_update,
427:                     platform.get_processor().get_key_store(),
428:                     platform.get_processor().get_account().storage_scheme,
429:                 )
430:                 .await
431:                 .change_context(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
432:                 .attach_printable("Unable to update payment intent")?;
433:         } else {
434:             split_pm_response_data
435:                 .secondary_payment_response_data
436:                 .push(payment_data);
437: 
438:             // Exit the loop if a payment failed
439:             break;
440:         }
441: 
442:         split_pm_response_data
443:             .secondary_payment_response_data
444:             .push(payment_data);
445:     }
446: 
447:     let payment_intent_update =
448:         hyperswitch_domain_models::payments::payment_intent::PaymentIntentUpdate::SplitPaymentStatusUpdate {
449:             status: split_pm_response_data.get_intent_status(),
450:             updated_by: platform
451:                 .get_processor()
452:                 .get_account()
453:                 .storage_scheme
454:                 .to_string(),
455:         };
456: 
457:     let _updated_payment_intent = db
458:         .update_payment_intent(
459:             payment_intent,
460:             payment_intent_update,
461:             platform.get_processor().get_key_store(),
462:             platform.get_processor().get_account().storage_scheme,
463:         )
464:         .await
465:         .change_context(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
466:         .attach_printable("Unable to update payment intent")?;
467: 
468:     split_pm_response_data.generate_response(
469:         &state,
470:         connector_http_status_code,
471:         external_latency,
472:         header_payload.x_hs_latency,
473:         &platform,
474:         &profile,
475:         Some(connector_response_data),
476:     )
477: }

<summary><h2> What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?</h2></summary>

Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in.

Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

<h3> Learn More About The Payment Modules </h3>
<details>

- **Cost Observability**  
  Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_

- **Revenue Recovery**  
  Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_

- **Vault**  
  A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_

- **Intelligent Routing**  
  Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_

- **Reconciliation**  
  Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_

- **Alternate Payment Methods**  
  Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_

</details>

## Why Hyperswitch?

Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations.

Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are.

<strong>“Linux for Payments”</strong> — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack.

We believe in:

- <strong> Embracing Payment Diversity:</strong> Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows.

- <strong> Open Source by Default:</strong> Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software.

- <strong> Community-Driven Development:</strong> Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. 

- <strong> Systems-Level Engineering:</strong> We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance.

- <strong> Maximizing Value Creation:</strong> For developers, customers, and partners alike.

- <strong> Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested:</strong> Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide.

What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?

 Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in. Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

Learn More About The Payment Modules

- **Cost Observability** Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_ - **Revenue Recovery** Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_ - **Vault** A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_ - **Intelligent Routing** Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_ - **Reconciliation** Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_ - **Alternate Payment Methods** Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_
## Quickstart

Local Setup via Docker

```bash # One-click local setup git clone --depth 1 --branch latest https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch cd hyperswitch scripts/setup.sh ```
This script: - Detects Docker/Podman - Offers multiple deployment profiles: - **Standard**: App server + Control Center - **Full**: Includes monitoring + schedulers - **Minimal**: Standalone App server - Provides access links when done If you need further help, check out our [video tutorial](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/overview/unified-local-setup-using-docker). 👉 After setup, [configure a connector](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/using-hyperswitch-control-center#add-a-payment-processor) and [test a payment](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/test-a-payment).

Hosted Sandbox (No Setup Required)

Hyperswitch offers a fully hosted sandbox environment that requires no setup. You can explore the Control Center, configure payment connectors, and test payments directly from the UI.
What you can do in the Hosted Sandbox - Access the full Control Center - Configure payment connectors - View logs, routing rules, and retry strategies - Try payments directly from the UI

Cloud Deployment

You can deploy to AWS, GCP, or Azure using Helm or CDK scripts. Fastest path: Click to deploy via AWS:
Cloud Deployment Instructions 1. Click the AWS deployment button above to launch the stack. 2. Follow the guided steps in the AWS Console (approx. 30–45 mins). ✅ This setup provisions Hyperswitch on your cloud account using CloudFormation. 📘 For full instructions and Helm-based deployments, check out the Cloud Install Guide.

Architectural Overview

 ## Why Hyperswitch? Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations. Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are. “Linux for Payments” — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack. We believe in: - Embracing Payment Diversity: Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows. - Open Source by Default: Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software. - Community-Driven Development: Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. - Systems-Level Engineering: We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance. - Maximizing Value Creation: For developers, customers, and partners alike. - Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested: Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide. ## Contributing We welcome contributors from around the world to help build Hyperswitch. Whether you're fixing bugs, improving documentation, or adding new features, your help is appreciated. Please read our [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started. Join the conversation on [Slack](https://inviter.co/hyperswitch-slack) or explore open issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/issues).
